strings: The Day After is an Alliance quest that bridges the survivors in Ironforge with researchers stationed in Dun Morogh. Gnoarn, lamenting the catastrophic radiation leak that cost him his legendary hair and his homeland, sends adventurers to assist Ozzie Togglevolt in Kharanos as he searches for a solution.

Gnomeregan's downfall took a deeply personal toll on every survivor, and Gnoarn is no exception. A refugee in Ironforge's Tinker Town, Gnoarn mourns not only the mechanical wonderland stolen by trogg invaders, but also his prized gnomefro—a glorious mane lost in an instant when a bolt of toxic fallout blasted him. Driven by lingering fury toward the troggs and a desperate hope to recover the city, he directs sympathetic travelers to colleagues who might still possess the scientific prowess to salvage what remains.

Rather than surrender to despair, Gnoarn points Alliance champions toward Kharanos, where inventive minds have begun tackling the fallout. Chief among them is Ozzie Togglevolt, working alongside his partner Razzle Sprysprocket. Ozzie remembers the horrifying moment of the catastrophe vividly, recalling how Gnoarn's locks fell out in clumps while madness and thirst for vengeance took hold. Now, in the relative safety of the snowbound town, Ozzie turns his engineering genius toward analyzing the contamination in hopes of finding an antidote.

Gnoarn is a gnome refugee found in Tinker Town in Ironforge. Deeply embittered by the trogg invasion and the city's radioactive vent catastrophe, he is especially traumatized by the sudden loss of his once-proud gnomefro.

Gnoarn believes there might still be hope to save Gnomeregan. Ozzie Togglevolt and his partner Razzle are stationed in Kharanos, conducting research into the toxic radiation clinging to the city and attempting to engineer a cure.

What happened to Gnomeregan to cause this?

During a massive subterranean invasion by barbaric troggs, High Tinker Gelbin Mekkatorque was persuaded to vent radioactive toxic waste into the lower halls to eradicate them. The gambit failed tragically, mutating or killing countless gnomes and rendering the techno-city unlivable without wiping out the troggs.

For gnomes, Gnoarn's peculiar lament captures the mixture of profound tragedy, eccentric pride, and bitter vengeance felt by every refugee exiled from their wondrous capital.

Gnoarn is fueled by personal fury and stubborn hope. The radioactive fallout that ruined Gnomeregan also stripped him of his pride and joy: the only gnomefro in all of Azeroth. Bitter over his baldness and burning for revenge against the invading troggs, he refuses to give up on his home. He believes that by directing able adventurers to Ozzie Togglevolt, there is still a chance to reverse the disaster and reclaim the city.

Deep in the Dwarven District of Stormwind, Shoni the Shilent is preparing a fleet of massive tunneling machines intended for transit to Dun Morogh. Stalled by a shortage of mechanical parts, she dispatches adventurers into the irradiated ruins of Gnomeregan to harvest intact gears and innards from rogue automatons.
A Fleet in Need of Guts

In Stormwind's Dwarven District, gnomish engineers work tirelessly to support their displaced kin. Among them is Shoni the Shilent, who oversees an ambitious subterranean venture: a fleet of gyrodrillmatic excavationators destined for Dun Morogh. The project faces a critical bottleneck, as she lacks the necessary components to get the massive digging rigs operational.

Rather than forge new parts from scratch, Shoni looks directly to the source of gnomish high technology: the lost city of Gnomeregan. The ruins and surrounding tunnels crawl with malfunctioning defense bots, mechanical sentries, and clockwork laborers roaming unchecked. Venturers are sent to pry apart these rogue machines and haul two dozen bundles of robo-mechanical guts back to human lands.

Bringing back two dozen mechanical guts provides enough scrap to patch together exactly one excavationator. With nearly four hundred machines remaining in her fleet, Shoni's dream of mass subterranean transport remains a monumental, agonizingly slow endeavor. Even so, every functioning machine represents a small step toward regaining ground lost in the cataclysm of Gnomeregan.

They are heavy gnomish tunneling rigs or mole machines designed for subterranean excavation and transport. Shoni the Shilent is attempting to assemble an entire fleet of them to move people or supplies to Dun Morogh.

The complex engineering of these subterranean tunneling vehicles requires precision gears, wiring, and actuators that are difficult to forge from scratch in Stormwind. By stripping functioning innards from the autonomous clockwork machines roaming Gnomeregan, she can salvage the vital spare parts needed to bring her grounded drilling rigs back online.

Cleansing the Eye is an Alliance quest that sends adventurers from the murky Wetlands south to the human capital of Stormwind. After recovering the cursed orb known as the Eye of Paleth, travelers must seek the aid of Archbishop Benedictus to purge its lingering taint.

The Eye of Paleth recovered from the marshlands does not shine with holy clarity. Instead, it is steeped in an unsettling shadow, bearing the residual sorrow and trauma of the terrible tragedy that unfolded where it was lost. The dwarf Glorin Steelbrow recognizes the power of the orb, but admits he lacks the divine craft to lift such a heavy affliction.

Because the Eyes of Paleth were originally fashioned by human priests of the Holy Light, only their highest order possesses the knowledge to undo the defilement. Glorin directs adventurers to journey to the kingdom of Stormwind and present the darkened orb to Archbishop Benedictus, leader of the Church of the Holy Light. Benedictus recognizes the immense danger of an unpurified relic and takes it upon himself to restore its sacred luminance.
What is the Eye of Paleth?

The Eyes of Paleth are sacred orbs crafted by human priests to shine with holy luminance. When untainted, their power aligns with the Holy Light, but if corrupted, their ambient energies become volatile and perilous.

According to Archbishop Benedictus, the orb bore witness to an immense, tragic event in the Wetlands, soaking up that agony over time. This lingering sorrow transformed into a corrupting curse that warped the relic's inherent power.

When the gnomes evacuated their irradiated capital, massive archives of vital technical knowledge and records were left behind. Master Mechanic Castpipe in Ironforge recruits daring operatives to infiltrate Gnomeregan and retrieve a high-security Prismatic Punch Card. Navigating through layers of computerized clearance, couriers must punch their way through progressively fortified terminals deep within the ruined city.

The sudden fall of Gnomeregan to troggs and deadly radiation forced the gnomish populace to abandon centuries of advanced research, schematics, and civic logs. Scattered throughout the technological corridors are Matrix Punchograph terminals, the automated data hubs that regulate security clearances and file storage. For exile leaders like Master Mechanic Castpipe, recovering these punch-encoded archives from the ruined depths represents one of the highest priorities of the refugee community in Tinker Town.

Gnomish data protocol demands rigorous clearance before granting access to central mainframes. Operating the system requires starting with a basic White Punch Card found among the wreckage outside the inner gates. Inserting it into a Matrix Punchograph 3005-A in the Train Depot produces a Yellow card, which must then be carried into the Dormitory's 3005-B terminal for a Blue upgrade, advanced through model 3005-C for a Red card, and finally brought down into the Engineering Labs to encode the coveted Prismatic Punch Card.

While Castpipe treats the quest as a matter of dire civic urgency, the actual punch cards feature binary data streams that reveal the eccentric, irreverent mindset of Gnomeregan's computing guilds. Amid genuine technical data, the punch patterns translate into humorous quips, absurd workplace complaints, and off-color jokes about High Tinker Gelbin Mekkatorque wearing night elven undergarments—demonstrating that even in the heart of high-tech infrastructure, gnome engineers could never resist a practical joke.
What is the Prismatic Punch Card?

The Prismatic Punch Card is the highest tier of security data card recognized by Gnomeregan's automated mainframes. It is created by processing a Red Punch Card at the Matrix Punchograph 3005-D terminal located deep inside the Engineering Labs.

Model 3005-A stands outside the instance in the Train Depot. Model 3005-B rests inside the Dormitory past the Clean Zone. Model 3005-C is situated on the catwalk platforms beyond, while Model 3005-D sits on the lower level of the Engineering Labs.

Castpipe's Task is an Alliance summons directing capable adventurers to seek out Master Mechanic Castpipe in Ironforge. Castpipe is coordinating perilous salvage operations into the irradiated ruins of Gnomeregan to extract vital mechanical and technical records. It serves as an official briefing that points mercenaries toward deep-retrieval missions inside the fallen city.

Following the tragic fall and subsequent radioactive quarantine of Gnomeregan, the surviving gnomes took refuge in Ironforge's Tinkertown. While their grand home remains overrun by troggs and irradiated constructs, crucial operational records and mechanical schematics are trapped deep within the city's surviving computing arrays. Recognizing that these files could prove invaluable to reclaiming or understanding what went wrong, Master Mechanic Castpipe began actively enlisting intrepid outsiders willing to brave the toxic halls.

Word of Castpipe's venture is spread by figures like Gaxim Rustfizzle of the Enlightened Assembly of Arcanology, Alchemy and Engineering Sciences. Though Castpipe is not a member of this esteemed academic body himself, fellow gnomes respect his technical acumen enough to endorse the effort. Rustfizzle's own calculations put the likelihood of Castpipe's mission having true strategic value at an encouraging eighty-four percent, motivating travelers to report to Tinkertown for orders.
Master Mechanic Castpipe is a respected gnomish engineer based in Tinkertown within Ironforge. He organizes salvage teams and data recovery operations focused on the subterranean ruins of Gnomeregan.

When Gnomeregan was contaminated and evacuated, vast amounts of critical technical knowledge, blueprints, and internal system logs were left behind in the mainframe memory. Retrieving this information is vital for the displaced gnomes hoping to rebuild.

Every recovery operation represents a fragment of your fallen home preserved from radiation and destruction, making Castpipe's mission a matter of cultural survival.

Given those favorable odds, Gaxim is eager to direct capable adventurers toward Ironforge to support the reclamation effort.

Nimboya wants the Witherbark trolls punished for betraying Thrall, though they were once allies of the Horde. Nimboya's pike is to carry Witherbark skulls and be planted in a Witherbark village in the Hinterlands.

Once the Witherbark trolls stood with the Horde, until they betrayed Thrall. Nimboya hands you a pike and sends you a long way north to the Hinterlands, northeast of Tarren Mill, the village held by the Forsaken. Hunt Witherbark trolls there and collect their skulls, then plant the pike in the ground in Hiri'watha or Zun'watha, two of their smaller villages, so they learn what their deeds cost. Afterwards Nimboya waits in Stranglethorn.

Troyas Moonbreeze found what looks like an ordinary stave in the rubble of the Feralas ruins, but he cannot shake the feeling there is more to it. He sends you to talk to his colleague Daryn Lightwind in Rut'theran Village.

Troyas Moonbreeze says the Feralas ruins are dangerous but have much to tell about what has happened there. A few days ago, searching the rubble to the south, he came upon a stave that seems ordinary, yet he cannot shake the feeling there is more to it. Troyas has a colleague in Darnassus who may be able to say what the stave is. He asks you to go and talk to her, Daryn Lightwind, in Rut'theran Village.

Daryn grumbles that Troyas keeps pestering her with wild notions that he has found something important. Ormer's Revenge begins the retributive campaign of Ormer Ironbraid, an explorer stranded high above the Whelgar Excavation Site in the Wetlands. After unearthing ancient fossilized bones, the dwarven dig team inadvertently drew packs of ravenous mottled raptors that slaughtered their companions and trapped the survivors on a rocky bluff.

The Whelgar Excavation Site was meant to be a triumph for dwarven archaeology, exposing massive prehistoric remains buried beneath the Wetlands muck. Instead, unearthing the colossal bones caught the attention of the marsh's native raptors. Drawn by the disturbance, packs of mottled predators swarmed the dig site, catching the excavators off guard and tearing through their ranks.

Only a handful of dwarves survived the initial slaughter.
